Hepatocellular Carcinoma: The presence of multifocal basophilic foci in the liver, high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, hyperchromatic nuclei, frequent mitotic figures, and local invasion into adjacent blood vessels are characteristic of hepatocellular carcinoma.
Hepatocellular Adenoma: The lack of a true capsule and the formation of a pseudo-capsule by hepatocyte sheets in the outer boundaries, as well as the presence of polygonal to short spindle-shaped cells, are features that can be seen in hepatocellular adenoma.
